subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Should the repository approve `contents: read` for both the primary and fallback GitHub App tokens solely to let the labeler fetch `.github/labeler.yml` without checking out repository content?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically correct and the hosted run passes, but granting repository-content access to credentials used by a `pull_request_target` automation workflow is a security-boundary choice that requires owner intent.

options.title: Approve scoped content read
options.body: Confirm that both App installations must fetch the repository labeler configuration and merge with the explicit read-only token scope retained.

options.title: Use a checked-out trusted config
options.body: Redesign the workflow to provide the trusted configuration file locally, then remove the App-token content-read requirement if that owner-approved architecture is preferable.

options.title: Pause pending App permission review
options.body: Hold the PR if either GitHub App should not receive repository-content access, even read-only access, in this workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped content read
recommendation.body: Confirm that both App installations must fetch the repository labeler configuration and merge with the explicit read-only token scope retained.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely owner for the repository-wide workflow permission boundary, although current local history could not be read conclusively in this review environment.
